 25| @jit(nopython=True, cache=True)
 26| def lcp_lemke(M, q, d=None, max_iter=10**6, piv_options=PivOptions(),
 27|               tableau=None, basis=None, z=None):
 28|     """
 29|     Solve the linear complementarity problem::
 30| 
 31|         z >= 0
 32|         M @ z + q >= 0
 33|         z @ (M @ z + q) = 0
 34| 
 35|     by Lemke's algorithm (with the lexicographic pivoting rule).
 36| 
 37|     Parameters
 38|     ----------
 39|     M : ndarray(float, ndim=2)
 40|         ndarray of shape (n, n).
 41| 
 42|     q : ndarray(float, ndim=1)
 43|         ndarray of shape (n,).
 44| 
 45|     d : ndarray(float, ndim=1), optional
 46|         Covering vector, ndarray of shape (n,). Must be strictly
 47|         positive. If None, default to vector of ones.
 48| 
 49|     max_iter : int, optional(default=10**6)
 50|         Maximum number of iteration to perform.
 51| 
 52|     piv_options : PivOptions, optional
 53|         PivOptions namedtuple to set the following tolerance values:
 54| 
 55|             fea_tol : float
 56|                 Feasibility tolerance (default={FEA_TOL}). (Not used in
 57|                 this function.)
 58| 
 59|             tol_piv : float
 60|                 Pivot tolerance (default={TOL_PIV}).
 61| 
 62|             tol_ratio_diff : float
 63|                 Tolerance used in the the lexicographic pivoting
 64|                 (default={TOL_RATIO_DIFF}).
 65| 
 66|     tableau : ndarray(float, ndim=2), optional
 67|         Temporary ndarray of shape (n, 2*n+2) to store the tableau.
 68|         Modified in place.
 69| 
 70|     basis : ndarray(int, ndim=1), optional
 71|         Temporary ndarray of shape (n,) to store the basic variables.
 72|         Modified in place.
 73| 
 74|     z : ndarray(float, ndim=1), optional
 75|         Output ndarray of shape (n,) to store the solution.
 76| 
 77|     Returns
 78|     -------
 79|     res : LCPResult
 80|         namedtuple consisting of the fields:
 81| 
 82|             z : ndarray(float, ndim=1)
 83|                 ndarray of shape (n,) containing the solution.
 84| 
 85|             success : bool
 86|                 True if the algorithm succeeded in finding a solution.
 87| 
 88|             status : int
 89|                 An integer representing the exit status of the result::
 90| 
 91|                     0 : Solution found successfully
 92|                     1 : Iteration limit reached
 93|                     2 : Secondary ray termination
 94| 
 95|             num_iter : int
 96|                 The number of iterations performed.
 97| 
 98|     Examples
 99|     --------
100|     >>> M = np.array([[1, 0, 0], [2, 1, 0], [2, 2, 1]])
101|     >>> q = np.array([-8, -12, -14])
102|     >>> res = lcp_lemke(M, q)
103|     >>> res.success
104|     True
105|     >>> res.z
106|     array([8., 0., 0.])
107|     >>> w = M @ res.z + q
108|     >>> w
109|     array([0., 4., 2.])
110|     >>> res.z @ w
111|     0.0
112| 
113|     References
114|     ----------
115|     * K. G. Murty, Linear Complementarity, Linear and Nonlinear
116|       Programming, 1988.
117| 
118|     """
119|     n = M.shape[0]
120| 
121|     success = False
122|     status = 1
123|     num_iter = 0
124| 
125|     if z is None:
126|         z = np.empty(n)
127| 
128|     if (q >= 0).all():  # Trivial case
129|         z[:] = 0
130|         success = True
131|         status = 0
132|         return LCPResult(z, success, status, num_iter)
133| 
134|     if d is None:
135|         d = np.ones(n)
136|     if tableau is None:
137|         tableau = np.empty((n, 2*n+2))
138|     if basis is None:
139|         basis = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int_)
140| 
141|     _initialize_tableau(M, q, d, tableau, basis)
142| 
143|     art_var = 2*n  # Artificial variable
144|     pivcol = art_var
145| 
146|     # Equivalent to lex_min_ratio_test
147|     pivrow = 0
148|     ratio_min = q[0] / d[0]
149|     for i in range(1, n):
150|         ratio = q[i] / d[i]
151|         if ratio <= ratio_min + piv_options.tol_ratio_diff:
152|             pivrow = i
153|             ratio = ratio_min
154| 
155|     _pivoting(tableau, pivcol, pivrow)
156|     basis[pivrow], pivcol = pivcol, pivrow + n
157|     num_iter += 1
158| 
159|     # Array to store row indices in lex_min_ratio_test
160|     argmins = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int_)
161| 
162|     while num_iter < max_iter:
163|         pivrow_found, pivrow = _lex_min_ratio_test(
164|             tableau, pivcol, 0, argmins,
165|             piv_options.tol_piv, piv_options.tol_ratio_diff
166|         )
167| 
168|         if not pivrow_found:  # Ray termination
169|             success = False
170|             status = 2
171|             break
172| 
173|         _pivoting(tableau, pivcol, pivrow)
174|         basis[pivrow], leaving_var = pivcol, basis[pivrow]
175|         num_iter += 1
176| 
177|         if leaving_var == art_var:  # Solution found
178|             success = True
179|             status = 0
180|             break
181|         elif leaving_var < n:
182|             pivcol = leaving_var + n
183|         else:
184|             pivcol = leaving_var - n
185| 
186|     _get_solution(tableau, basis, z)
187| 
188|     return LCPResult(z, success, status, num_iter)
189|

196| @jit(nopython=True, cache=True)
197| def _initialize_tableau(M, q, d, tableau, basis):
198|     """
199|     Initialize the `tableau` and `basis` arrays in place.
200| 
201|     With covering vector d and artificial variable z0, the LCP is
202|     written as
203| 
204|         q = w - M z - d z0
205| 
206|     where the variables are ordered as (w, z, z0). Thus,
207|     `tableaus[:, :n]` stores I, `tableaus[:, n:2*n]` stores -M,
208|     `tableaus[:, 2*n]` stores -d, and `tableaus[:, -1]` stores q, while
209|     `basis` stores 0, ..., n-1 (variables w).
210| 
211|     Parameters
212|     ----------
213|     M : ndarray(float, ndim=2)
214|         ndarray of shape (n, n).
215| 
216|     q : ndarray(float, ndim=1)
217|         ndarray of shape (n,).
218| 
219|     d : ndarray(float, ndim=1)
220|         ndarray of shape (n,).
221| 
222|     tableau : ndarray(float, ndim=2)
223|         Empty ndarray of shape (n, 2*n+2) to store the tableau.
224|         Modified in place.
225| 
226|     basis : ndarray(int, ndim=1)
227|         Empty ndarray of shape (n,) to store the basic variables.
228|         Modified in place.
229| 
230|     Returns
231|     -------
232|     tableau : ndarray(float, ndim=2)
233|         View to `tableau`.
234| 
235|     basis : ndarray(int, ndim=1)
236|         View to `basis`.
237| 
238|     """
239|     n = M.shape[0]
240| 
241|     tableau[:n, :n] = 0
242|     for i in range(n):
243|         tableau[i, i] = 1
244| 
245|     for i in range(n):
246|         for j in range(n):
247|             tableau[i, n+j] = -M[i, j]
248| 
249|     for i in range(n):
250|         tableau[i, 2*n] = -d[i]
251| 
252|     for i in range(n):
253|         tableau[i, -1] = q[i]
254| 
255|     for i in range(n):
256|         basis[i] = i
257| 
258|     return tableau, basis
259| 
260| 
261| @jit(nopython=True, cache=True)
262| def _get_solution(tableau, basis, z):
263|     """
264|     Fetch the solution from `tableau` and `basis`.
265| 
266|     Parameters
267|     ----------
268|     tableau : ndarray(float, ndim=2)
269|         ndarray of shape (n, 2*n+2) containing the terminal tableau.
270| 
271|     basis : ndarray(int, ndim=1)
272|         ndarray of shape (n,) containing the terminal basis.
273| 
274|     z : ndarray(float, ndim=1)
275|         Empty ndarray of shape (n,) to store the solution. Modified in
276|         place.
277| 
278|     Returns
279|     -------
280|     z : ndarray(float, ndim=1)
281|         View to `z`.
282| 
283|     """
284|     n = z.size
285| 
286|     z[:] = 0
287|     for i in range(n):
288|         if n <= basis[i] < 2*n:
289|             z[basis[i]-n] = tableau[i, -1]
290| 
291|     return z
